tests.mutation: In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make offered two melee attacks (`Attacks: 2`); this test went red and no other did.
In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make ignored whether the attacker can see the creature (`if (false && sight.CannotSee)`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make consulted avoidance only for a creature leaving by its action (`&& leaving.Means == DepartureMeans.OwnAction`), so Disengage, a Teleport and an explosion all provoked; this test went red and no other did.
In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make ignored a spent Reaction (`if (false && !reaction.Available)`); this test went red and no other did.
In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make ignored the Incapacitated condition (`if (false && incapacitated.Incapacitated)`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make answered for a creature leaving reach by none of the means the glossary lists (`if (false && leaving.Means == DepartureMeans.ByNoneOfThose)`); this test went red and no other did.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; the OpportunityAttack handler defaulted a missing Reaction statement (`request.Reaction ?? ReactionAvailability.Has("default")`); this test went red and no other did. It went red too when a missing Incapacitated statement defaulted, and when the OpportunityAttackAvoidance handler defaulted a missing LeavingReach.

In a throwaway copy, net10.0 suite run; OpportunityAttackRules.Make dropped the avoidance verdict's decisions from the offer (`OpportunityAttackOffer.None(verdict.Because, verdict.Authority)`), so a refusal resting on the engine's decision named none; this test went red and no other did.
